subject: MAP gating: units-per-dollar operational acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Samir Ahmed <samir@mediflow.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP gating: tokens/$, caching & batching clarifications

Hannah —

Thanks for the call earlier. As we build the MAP and the evaluation plan, procurement needs a concise acceptance checklist for the units-per-dollar assumptions. High level items we care about:

- Tokens per call: our median prompt+response is ~650 tokens (sample attached), peak at ~2,400 tokens for long transcripts.
- Concurrency/profile: we expect 40 sustained qps for the pilot region, spikes to 120qps for 90s.
- Caching behavior: can Redwood do prefix/KV caching at the route-level and what is expected cache hit rate on our workload?
- Batching: what practical batching sizes can preserve our 200ms P95 latency SLO for chat flows?

Can you put together a short ops acceptance checklist that we can attach to the MAP (so procurement has concrete gating criteria)? Also include any recommended smoke tests we should run during the eval window so we can validate tokens/$ assumptions.

Appreciate it — Samir

Attachment: mediflow_traffic_sample.csv (sample payloads & token counts)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Ahmed <samir@mediflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP gating: tokens/$, caching & batching clarifications

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask. I sketched an operational acceptance checklist that we can embed in the MAP and use as gating criteria for the eval. High-level approach: three validation tracks (cost modeling, ops smoke, SLA fit).

Draft checklist (short):

1) Cost reconciliation
   - Run 24h shadow run against sample traffic (attached) to measure tokens/response and tokens/$ at current config.
   - Confirm tokens-per-response median/90/99 and estimated $/1M tokens.

2) Caching & batching verification
   - Validate KV/prefix cache reduces avg tokens generated by >= 12% on representative prefix-heavy flows (target hit-rate 25%+).
   - Measure batching latency trade-offs: run batch sizes [1, 4, 8] and capture P50/P95 for short (<=700 tokens) and long flows.

3) Latency and degradation policy
   - Confirm P95 <= 200ms for short chat paths at production concurrency target using dedicated capacity; define fallback to smaller model variant if breach occurs.

4) Ops artifacts
   - Upload smoke-test spec, results, and token-accounting report to shared Drive link.

I'll loop in Karthik and Ben to turn this into a runnable spec with concrete test steps and an estimated timeline for the MAP eval window. Can you confirm the pilot region and a target signoff date (you mentioned wanting this closed in September)?

— Hannah

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP gating: tokens/$, caching & batching clarifications

Hannah / all —

I drafted the ops smoke test checklist (short form) below. I'll push the runnable scripts to the shared Drive after quick internal validation. Concrete test cases and pass criteria:

Ops smoke checklist (summary):

A) Shadow run (24h)
   - Run customer traffic in shadow mode at 1x and 2x nominal rate to capture token counts and cache effectiveness.
   - Output: token-usage.csv, per-route tokens summary, cost projection (tokens -> $ at hosted rate and dedicated estimate).

B) Caching verification
   - Seed KV/prefix cache with representative prefixes.
   - Target: cache-hit >= 25% on flows flagged as prefix-heavy (we'll use the sample CSV to find those).
   - Measure reduction in generated tokens and delta to cost projection.

C) Batching latency sweep
   - Sweep batch sizes 1, 4, 8 on short flows (<=700 tokens) and long flows (>700 tokens).
   - Pass if P95 latency delta between batch=1 and chosen batch <= 80ms and P95 overall <= 200ms for short flows at expected concurrency.

D) Fallback behavior
   - Trigger a simulated capacity pressure event to validate automatic fallback to smaller model variant (no data loss, errors < 0.1%).

E) Deliverables
   - ops-smoke-results.zip (logs + CSVs), token-accounting-report.pdf, and a short readout (5 slides).

I'll include the commands to run locally and a Kubernetes job definition for the dedicated pool. ETA to push artifacts: EOD today.

— Ben

Hannah / Ben —

1) Can we get an estimated tokens-per-1000-requests table for the three batch configs (1/4/8) using our sample? Procurement needs that for quick cost math.
2) Can the MAP include a closing milestone that requires the ops-smoke-results.zip and token-accounting-report.pdf to be uploaded and signed off by both parties before SOW signature?

We can run the shadow traffic as soon as you drop the scripts. Proposed timeline:
- 9/19–9/20: shadow run + caching/batching sweep
- 9/22: readout and token-accounting upload
- 9/24: mutual sign-off and procurement SOW trigger

If you can add the small table and the explicit sign-off clause to the MAP draft, we can move to signatures on the proposed schedule.

Best — Samir
